title: Cops cleared in fatal shooting of Burk's Falls woman
subtitle: One officer fired his gun four times at the woman while at the same time the other officer shot his gun three times
article: Two OPP officers have been cleared by the SIU in connection with fatally shooting 38-year-old Sheena Jackson last August in Burk's Falls.
On August 5, 2021, OPP Almaguin Highlands Detachment officers went to a cottage at Ye Olde Cutter Camp in Burk's Falls for a disturbance call.
There, the officers came across the woman who swung a knife through the open driver's door window of their cruiser, says a news release today from the SIU.

"This was followed by the woman advancing towards an officer with the knife. The woman ignored repeated commands for her to drop the weapon. One officer fired his gun four times at the woman while at the same time the other officer shot his gun three times. The woman was struck four times and fell to the ground. The officers provided CPR while waiting for paramedics to arrive. The woman was pronounced deceased at the scene."

SIU Director Joe Martino says he is "satisfied that the officers acted reasonably when they sought to protect themselves from a potentially lethal attack with a resort to lethal force of their own, leaving no basis for proceeding with criminal charges in this case."

"The situation in which the officers found themselves also persuades me that their resort to gunfire was not unreasonable," said Martino. "The Complainant had in her possession a knife with a blade of some ten centimetres in length, clearly capable of causing death as she neared to within five metres of the officers. She had also shown a propensity to use it, seconds earlier having attacked another officer with the knife. Retreat or withdrawal were not realistic options in the circumstances."
Martino said that one officer declined to be interviewed or to provide notes, as is his legal right. A second officer was Interviewed, but declined to submit notes.

At autopsy, the pathologist attributed the death to 'gunshot wounds'. It remains unclear which of the shots fired caused which wound, and whether both or only one of the officers discharged the shots that resulted in the woman's death.
